title: Faerie
sourceNote: Based on the supplied Faerie 2.0 cards. This is a studio reference, not an original author rule sheet.

sections.heading: Prepare the market
sections.text: Use all 40 physical Faerie cards, including repeated copies. Combine this half-deck with another compatible 40-card half-deck and use the normal base-game market setup. Keep your starting deck and the permanent supply separate.

sections.heading: Choices and costs
sections.text: When a card says Choose one, select one listed option. A triangle separates an action or cost from its result: complete the required part before receiving the benefit. Check the exact target and quantity on the card.

sections.heading: Example: Gremlin
sections.text: Its first option requires you to discard a card from your hand to gain two influence. Its second option requires you to devour Gremlin itself to gain three influence. Devouring is different from discarding: the devoured card is removed from the game and does not return when your discard pile is shuffled.

sections.heading: Example: Tasha, the Demonologist
sections.text: Choose between four power; recruiting a market card of the Ambition aspect or Demon type costing five or less for free; or recruiting Graz'zt for free. These are alternatives, not three effects gained together. The special recruitment options still require the named or qualifying card to be available.

sections.heading: During play
sections.text: Resolve deployment, returning troops or spies, recruitment and promotion using the base-game rules unless the played card explicitly changes them. Distinguish a card's aspect from its creature type when checking a condition. The italic flavour text is not an effect. Use the current printed card text for individual exceptions.

title: Siege
sourceNote: Based on the supplied Siege cards and the author's introduction. This is a studio reference, not an original author rule sheet.

sections.heading: Prepare the market
sections.text: Use all 40 physical Siege cards, including duplicates, together with another compatible 40-card half-deck. Follow the normal setup for the market, starting decks and permanent supply. Siege is a market half-deck, not a separate map or game mode.

sections.heading: What changes
sections.text: The author designed Siege around varied card interactions and alternative playstyles, with relatively limited resource generation. Its individual card effects supply the exceptions to normal play; there is no separate siege phase to introduce.

sections.heading: Example: Avatar of Lolth
sections.text: Choose one option. Either place a spy and then draw a card, or return one of your spies to place another played card, or a card from your discard pile, on top of your deck. For the second option, returning your spy is the requirement before you receive the effect.

sections.heading: Example: Relentless Siege
sections.text: Gain the three influence shown on the card. For the rest of that turn, treat other players' troops as white troops as instructed. This is a temporary effect: it ends with the turn and does not permanently change ownership of those troops.

sections.heading: Check each effect
sections.text: Read whether an effect targets your troop, an enemy troop, a white troop or a spy. Do not treat these as interchangeable unless the card says so. Follow any printed order of actions and pay a requirement before the effect after its triangle. Normal presence rules and base-game action costs continue to apply unless explicitly overridden.

sections.heading: After the turn
sections.text: Complete the base game's normal end-of-turn procedure. Do not carry temporary permissions or unused turn resources into the next player's turn. Keep the played card available to read whenever a conditional effect needs clarification.

title: Svirfneblin & Kuo-Toa
sourceNote: Studio summary of the author's expansion overview and supplied v1.1 update pack; individual card wording takes priority.

sections.heading: Two separate half-decks
sections.text: The complete expansion contains two 40-card half-decks. Each can be paired with another compatible half-deck using the usual market setup.

sections.heading: Svirfneblin: Betrayal
sections.text: Effects interact with inner circles: promotion may benefit another player, while other abilities return or play promoted cards. Read the required owner, destination and cost carefully. Trading inner-circle points for a powerful immediate effect is part of this deck's design.

sections.heading: Kuo-Toa: Persistence
sections.text: Certain cards remain in play across turns, following their printed effects. Reshuffling your deck ends their persistence; some opposing effects can force a reshuffle or remove a persistent card sooner. Resolve the exact timing on each card.

sections.heading: Combining decks
sections.text: The author recommends removing Blue Dragon when pairing Dragons with Betrayal. Aberration discard effects can be especially punishing alongside Betrayal. Learn each half-deck separately before combining the two new halves.

sections.heading: What this library pack contains
sections.text: The supplied v1.1 update sheets contain 18 replacement cards and card backs. They update an existing set; they are not the complete 80-card expansion. Replace the corresponding older cards rather than adding extra copies.
